results.name: yes_rate_drift_early_minus_late
results.description: Yes rate on trials with trial_index < 150 minus yes rate on trials with trial_index >= 300; observed above null means people grow more conservative over the session than the stationary model predicts.
results.code:
# name: yes_rate_drift_early_minus_late
# description: Yes rate on trials with trial_index < 150 minus yes rate on trials with trial_index >= 300; observed above null means people grow more conservative over the session than the stationary model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(int)
    a = r[ti < 150].mean()
    b = r[ti >= 300].mean()
    return float(0.0 if (np.isnan(a) or np.isnan(b)) else a - b)

results.name: last_digit_rule_with_one_exception
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets whose final digit matches exactly 3 of 4 examples (a final-digit rule with one exception, e.g. 71,61,26,81 -> 11); observed above null means people tolerate an exception to a rule more than the model's 10% stray rate allows.
results.code:
# name: last_digit_rule_with_one_exception
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets whose final digit matches exactly 3 of 4 examples (a final-digit rule with one exception, e.g. 71,61,26,81 -> 11); observed above null means people tolerate an exception to a rule more than the model's 10% stray rate allows.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    k = x.mod(10).eq(t % 10, axis=0).sum(axis=1)
    m = (n == 4) & (k == 3) & ~isin
    v = r[m].mean()
    return float(0.0 if np.isnan(v) else v)

results.name: near_first_minus_near_last_example
results.description: Among sets with 2+ examples and non-example targets, yes rate for targets within 5 of the FIRST shown example minus yes rate for targets within 5 of the LAST shown example; observed above null means the first example anchors generalization more than the model (which only uses last-step heading) predicts.
results.code:
# name: near_first_minus_near_last_example
# description: Among sets with 2+ examples and non-example targets, yes rate for targets within 5 of the FIRST shown example minus yes rate for targets within 5 of the LAST shown example; observed above null means the first example anchors generalization more than the model (which only uses last-step heading) predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    first = x[0]
    last = x.ffill(axis=1).iloc[:, -1]
    base = (n >= 2) & ~isin
    nf = base & ((t - first).abs() <= 5) & ((t - last).abs() > 5)
    nl = base & ((t - last).abs() <= 5) & ((t - first).abs() > 5)
    a = r[nf].mean()
    b = r[nl].mean()
    return float(0.0 if (np.isnan(a) or np.isnan(b)) else a - b)

results.name: two_example_far_extrapolation
results.description: For two-example sets, yes rate for targets more than 15 beyond the nearer end of the span (above max+15 or below min-15); observed above null means people extrapolate far beyond a pair of examples more than the model predicts.

# description: For two-example sets, yes rate for targets more than 15 beyond the nearer end of the span (above max+15 or below min-15); observed above null means people extrapolate far beyond a pair of examples more than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)

results.name: single_example_distance_gradient
results.description: For one-example sets, yes rate for targets within 10 of the example (excluding the example) minus yes rate for targets more than 30 away; observed above null means a steeper similarity falloff from a lone example than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: single_example_distance_gradient
# description: For one-example sets, yes rate for targets within 10 of the example (excluding the example) minus yes rate for targets more than 30 away; observed above null means a steeper similarity falloff from a lone example than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    d = (t - x[0]).abs()
    one = (n == 1) & ~isin
    a = r[one & (d <= 10)].mean()
    b = r[one & (d > 30)].mean()
    return float(0.0 if (np.isnan(a) or np.isnan(b)) else a - b)

results.name: wide_span_interior_yes_4ex
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets strictly inside the span of 4-example sets whose span (max-min) is at least 50; observed above null means people fill in wide scattered sets as a broad range more than the model predicts, below means less.

# name: wide_span_interior_yes_4ex
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets strictly inside the span of 4-example sets whose span (max-min) is at least 50; observed above null means people fill in wide scattered sets as a broad range more than the model predicts, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)

    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)

results.name: same_parity_set_parity_match_yes
results.description: For sets of 3+ examples that are all even or all odd, yes rate for non-example targets with that same parity; observed below null means the model over-applies the odd/even rule (e.g. 70,10,88,40 -> 48) relative to people.
results.code:
# name: same_parity_set_parity_match_yes
# description: For sets of 3+ examples that are all even or all odd, yes rate for non-example targets with that same parity; observed below null means the model over-applies the odd/even rule (e.g. 70,10,88,40 -> 48) relative to people.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    par = x.mod(2)
    allsame = (par.max(axis=1) == par.min(axis=1)) & (n >= 3)
    m = allsame & ((t % 2) == par[0]) & ~isin
    v = r[m].mean()
    return float(0.0 if np.isnan(v) else v)
